data.narrative:
Star Catcher, a Series A space and aerospace company founded by Andrew Rush, Michael Snyder, and Bryan Lyandvert, has raised $88M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of five public-sector peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight private-stage companies including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, anchoring assessments within the frontier space technology segment.

Two methods triangulate a valuation range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $88M raised proxy, implying $176M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies yields a $1.3B median valuation, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B (Starcloud at low end, Cowboy Space Corporation at high end). Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples is not applicable; the target's revenue is not disclosed, precluding meaningful multiple application against the 24.4x median P/S observed across public Space & Aerospace names.

The triangulated range is $150M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median of $738M across the two applicable methods. This wide range reflects material uncertainty in stage-comparable positioning and peer alignment within a heterogeneous private aerospace cohort. Key drivers of valuation placement within this band include revenue scale, customer traction, and technological differentiation relative to the identified peer set—factors not quantified in available data.
